title.en: Tests of adequacy of index numbers

heading.en: Is the index a good one?

title.en: State the unit, time reversal and factor reversal tests
Verify the tests for given data
Explain why Fisher's index is ideal

say.en: If prices doubled from 2015 to 2025, then going back from 2025 to 2015 they must halve. Does every formula agree? Tests of adequacy check this. In this lesson: State the unit, time reversal and factor reversal tests.
Verify the tests for given data.
Explain why Fisher's index is ideal.

body.en: Unit test: the index should not depend on the units in which prices are quoted (all except the simple aggregative index pass). Time reversal test: $P_{01} \times P_{10} = 1$ (indices as ratios). Factor reversal test: $P_{01} \times Q_{01} = V_{01} = \frac{\sum p_1 q_1}{\sum p_0 q_0}$. Fisher's index satisfies both reversal *tests*, so it is called the ideal index number. Laspeyres' and Paasche's satisfy neither; Marshall–Edgeworth and Kelly satisfy the time reversal test only.

narration.en: The time reversal test asks that P zero one times P one zero equals one. The factor reversal test asks that the price index times the quantity index equals the value index. Fisher's index passes both, so it is ideal.
narration.kn: ಸಮಯ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಯ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ: P₀₁ × P₁₀ = 1. ಅಂಶ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಯ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ: ಬೆಲೆ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ × ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ = ಮೌಲ್ಯ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ. ಫಿಶರ್ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ ಎರಡನ್ನೂ ಪೂರೈಸುವುದರಿಂದ ಅದು ಆದರ್ಶ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ.

explanation.en: Only Fisher's ideal index satisfies both the time reversal and the factor reversal tests. Marshall–Edgeworth, Kelly's, the simple aggregative index and the simple GM of relatives satisfy the time reversal test only. Laspeyres', Paasche's, Dorbish–Bowley and the simple AM of relatives satisfy neither.

problem.en: For the four-item data (p₀ = [40, 80, 20, 100], q₀ = [10, 5, 20, 4], p₁ = [60, 100, 30, 120], q₁ = [12, 6, 18, 5]), show that Fisher's index satisfies the factor reversal test.

steps.en: P₀₁ × Q₀₁ = 1.5375 = 2,460/1,600 = V₀₁. Hence FRT is satisfied.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. For the four-item data (p₀ = [40, 80, 20, 100], q₀ = [10, 5, 20, 4], p₁ = [60, 100, 30, 120], q₁ = [12, 6, 18, 5]), show that Fisher's index satisfies the factor reversal test.

say.en: Let us work this out together. For the four-item data (p 0 = [40, 80, 20, 100], q 0 = [10, 5, 20, 4], p 1 = [60, 100, 30, 120], q 1 = [12, 6, 18, 5]), show that Fisher's index satisfies the factor reversal test.
Σp 0q 0 equals 1,600, Σp 1q 0 equals 2,180, Σp 0q 1 equals 1,820, Σp 1q 1 equals 2,460.
P 01 equals the square root of (2,180 over 1,600 times 2,460 over 1,820) equals 1.3571.
Q 01 equals the square root of (1,820 over 1,600 times 2,460 over 2,180) equals 1.1330.
P 01 times Q 01 equals 1.5375 equals 2,460 over 1,600 equals V 01. Hence FRT is satisfied.
So the answer is P 01 times Q 01 equals V 01 equals 1.5375.

body.en: Remember: Fisher passes the time reversal and factor reversal tests. Laspeyres' and Paasche's pass neither reversal test.
